prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests with 406 when the Accept header lists only `application/json` (without also listing `text/event-stream`), even though JSON response mode never streams SSE and shouldn't require that header. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests with 406 when the Accept header lists only `application/json` (without also listing `text/event-stream`), even though JSON response mode never streams SSE and shouldn't require that header. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same Accept-header validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts and fix the same 406 rejection. #1996 adds a dedicated `acceptsMediaType` helper that does proper media-range parsing per RFC 7231 (splits on ';', strips parameters, excludes entries with q=0, compares type/subtype tokens). #2046 instead does a plain `acceptHeader.includes('application/json')` substring check, which both ignores `q=0` exclusion (a client explicitly disabling JSON via `application/json;q=0` would still pass) and is vulnerable to false-positive substring matches against other media types that contain that string (e.g. `application/json-seq`, `application/json-patch+json`). #1996's parsing approach handles these edge cases correctly where #2046's does not.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same Accept-header validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts and fix the same 406 rejection. #1996 adds a dedicated `acceptsMediaType` helper that does proper media-range parsing per RFC 7231 (splits on ';', strips parameters, excludes entries with q=0, compares type/subtype tokens). #2046 instead does a plain `acceptHeader.includes('application/json')` substring check, which both ignores `q=0` exclusion (a client explicitly disabling JSON via `application/json;q=0` would still pass) and is vulnerable to false-positive substring matches against other media types that contain that string (e.g. `application/json-seq`, `application/json-patch+json`). #1996's parsing approach handles these edge cases correctly where #2046's does not.
